text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- British Minister for Overseas Development Lynda Chalker acknowledges Nigeria's efforts at democratisation; her Canadian counterpart canvasses for dialogue with its military government after meeting of Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group on Nigeria in London.
- Work on expanding telephone exchanges of Nigerian Telecommunications Limited stalled since last year when World Bank withdrew a loan of $225 million for the project.

- U.S. President Bill Clinton hails military ruler General Sani Abacha for "his remarkable leadership of Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) and his personal commitment to Liberian peace process", says an envoy of Clinton to Abacha in the Nigerian capital Abuja on Tuesday.

- Nigerian Liquefied Natural Gas Company rejects idea of out-of-court settlement with Italian state utility firm Enel which pulled out from a contract to buy Nigerian gas and insists on arbitration proceedings.
- Investors are jostling for substantial stakes in the big four banks following expectations of improved dividend from their proposed recapitalisation.
- Russia, Iraq seek diamond and oil pacts, respectively, with Nigeria.
- British trade mission of oil and gas firms to visit Nigerian oil sector next month.
- Strong demand for shares raises prices of food and beverage stocks as well as insurance stocks.
- Nigerian-born Commonwealth secretary-general Emeka Anyaoku has moved from Nigeria to Botswana a planned African meeting to reflect on democracy.

- Electoral commission NECON issued close to 60 million cards for registration of voters for elections in the transition to civil rule plan of the military government which ended on Wednesday after 10 days
- Petroleum Trust Fund, which is disbursing proceeds of a 1994 pump price hike on social projects, says it will spend 2.3 billion naira to rehabilitate and expand four water schemes in Lagos.
- Nigerian government restates its commitment to complete the troubled Ajaokuta steel project in central Nigeria.
